title: Why Does My Dog Sunbathe Even When It's Already Hot?
description:
Your dog is stretched out in a sunbeam on a warm day, and it looks uncomfortable, but it's not. Here's what's actually going on.

script: Your dog is stretched out flat in a sunbeam on a day that's already warm, and it looks like it should be uncomfortable, but it almost never is. Dogs regulate their body temperature very differently than we do, they don't sweat through their skin the way humans do, so a patch of direct sunlight doesn't overheat them nearly as fast as you'd expect, especially with a light breeze or airflow nearby. Sunlight also triggers a real physiological response, it helps their body produce vitamin D, and it just feels good on tight or achy muscles, which is part of why older dogs in particular tend to seek it out. There's also a simple comfort factor, warm ground and warm air on bare skin is genuinely pleasant, the same reason we don't mind lying on a beach towel in the heat. The only time to actually worry is if a dog can't move away from the sun on its own, has no shade or water nearby, or shows heavy panting and lethargy, that's a real heat risk. But a dog voluntarily choosing a sunny spot for a nap is just a dog doing exactly what feels good.
